statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol or Drugs
elements: Drove or was in actual physical control of a moving vehicle
On a public road, highway, or private property open to the public
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs to the extent it was less safe to drive
OR with BAC of 0.08% or more (0.04% for CDL holders; 0.02% for drivers under 21)
mandatory_minimum: 24 hours jail (1st); 72 hours jail (2nd); 15 days jail (3rd felony)
enhancements: Child under 14 in vehicle: additional misdemeanor under O.C.G.A. § 40-6-391(l)
BAC 0.15% or higher: mandatory ignition interlock device
3rd offense within 10 years: felony classification
4th+ offense: felony regardless of look-back period
notes: Administrative license suspension (ALS) separate from criminal penalties. Implied consent under § 40-5-55 requires chemical test.

elements: First DUI conviction within 10-year look-back period
Drove or was in actual physical control of a moving vehicle
Under influence to extent less safe to drive OR BAC 0.08%+
mandatory_minimum: 24 hours jail; 40 hours community service; 12 months probation; DUI Risk Reduction Program
enhancements: BAC 0.15%+: ignition interlock device required
Child passenger under 14: child endangerment charge added
notes: License suspended 1 year. Minimum 24 hours must be served; balance may be probated. Clinical evaluation required.

elements: Prior DUI conviction(s) within applicable look-back period
Drove or was in actual physical control of a moving vehicle
Under influence to extent less safe OR BAC 0.08%+
mandatory_minimum: 72 hours mandatory jail (2nd); 15 days mandatory jail (3rd felony)
enhancements: Habitual violator designation possible on 3rd offense
Ignition interlock mandatory on 2nd+ offense
5-year license revocation on habitual violator designation
notes: 10-year look-back period for felony classification on 3rd offense. 4th offense is always felony.

statute_title: DUI — Under the Influence of Drugs
elements: Drove or was in actual physical control of a moving vehicle
Under the influence of any controlled substance, marijuana, or other drug
To the extent it was less safe to drive
OR per se: blood or urine shows presence of Schedule I-IV controlled substance under § 40-6-391(a)(6)
mandatory_minimum: 24 hours jail (1st offense)
enhancements: Any prior DUI within 10 years elevates penalties
Drug paraphernalia in vehicle: additional charges
notes: Per se DUI-drugs: any detectable amount of Schedule I-IV substance in blood/urine — no impairment proof required.

elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
On a public road, highway, or private property open to the public
In reckless disregard for the safety of persons or property
enhancements: Resulting serious injury or death: vehicular homicide charges under § 40-6-393
Repeat offense: points accumulation leads to license suspension
notes: 4 points assessed on driver's license. Frequently charged alongside DUI.

statute_title: Duty to Stop at or Return to Scene of Accident
elements: Defendant was operating a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to immediately stop at or return to the scene
Defendant failed to provide identifying information and render reasonable aid
enhancements: Death resulting: minimum 3 years imprisonment
Serious injury: minimum 1 year imprisonment
notes: Duty to stop, render aid, and exchange information. Property-damage-only hit-and-run is misdemeanor.

penalty_max: 15 years (1st degree felony); 12 months (2nd degree misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
In violation of O.C.G.A. § 40-6-391 (DUI), racing, or fleeing statute
Such violation was the proximate cause of death of another person
mandatory_minimum: 3 years for 1st degree
enhancements: Multiple deaths: consecutive sentences possible
DUI-related: mandatory minimum 3 years
notes: 1st degree requires underlying DUI, racing, or fleeing as predicate. 2nd degree involves other traffic violations.

statute_title: Homicide by Vehicle in the Second Degree
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
In violation of a traffic law other than DUI, racing, or fleeing
Such violation was the proximate cause of death of another person
enhancements: Reckless driving as predicate: potential 1st degree elevation
notes: Second-degree homicide by vehicle covers negligent or traffic-violation-related deaths that don't involve DUI or racing.

statute_title: Driving on Suspended or Revoked License
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public road
Defendant's driver's license or privilege to drive was suspended or revoked
Defendant had actual or constructive knowledge of the suspension
mandatory_minimum: 2 days jail (1st); 10 days (2nd); felony 3rd offense
enhancements: Habitual violator under § 40-5-58: felony with 5-year revocation
Driving during DUI-related suspension: aggravated penalty
notes: Habitual violator: 3rd major violation within 5 years = 5-year revocation and felony charge.

statute_title: Fleeing or Attempting to Elude a Police Officer
elements: Law enforcement officer gave a visible or audible signal to stop
Officer was in uniform or marked vehicle
Defendant willfully failed or refused to stop or fled
enhancements: High-speed chase endangering others: felony under § 40-6-395(b)
Serious injury or death: vehicular homicide charges added
notes: Aggravated form charged when driver travels 30+ mph over limit, enters oncoming traffic, or runs traffic control devices.

statute_title: Open Container of Alcoholic Beverage in Motor Vehicle
elements: Defendant operated or was a passenger in a moving vehicle on a public highway
An open container of alcohol was possessed or accessible in the passenger area
Container had been opened or had broken seal or partially removed contents
notes: Locked trunk or locked glove box exempted. Does not apply to passengers in chartered buses, taxis, or limousines.

statute_title: Refusal of Chemical Test — Implied Consent
offense_class: Administrative (license suspension); refusal admissible at trial
penalty_max: 1-year license suspension (1st refusal); 3-year suspension (2nd refusal within 5 years)
elements: Defendant was lawfully arrested for DUI
Law enforcement officer read the Georgia Implied Consent Notice
Defendant refused to submit to the designated chemical test
enhancements: 2nd refusal within 5 years: 3-year license suspension
notes: Refusal admissible as evidence of consciousness of guilt at trial. No standalone criminal charge; triggers administrative ALS.

penalty_max: 15 years (Schedule I-II, 1st offense); 30 years (2nd offense); 5 years (Schedule III-V)
elements: Defendant knowingly and willfully possessed a controlled substance
Substance was listed on the Georgia controlled substance schedule
Defendant had actual or constructive possession
enhancements: Near school, park, or public housing within 1,000 feet: mandatory 2-year add-on
Large quantity: trafficking presumption under § 16-13-31
Prior drug conviction: enhanced maximum
notes: Marijuana treated separately under § 16-13-2. Trafficking thresholds trigger mandatory minimums under § 16-13-31.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (1 oz or less); Felony (more than 1 oz)
penalty_max: 12 months (1 oz or less); 10 years (1 oz to 10 lbs)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
Amount was 1 oz or less (misdemeanor) or more than 1 oz (felony)
Possession was knowing and willful
enhancements: More than 10 lbs: trafficking under § 16-13-31 with mandatory minimums
Near drug-free school zone: enhanced penalty
notes: Medical marijuana oil (low-THC cannabis oil) permitted under § 16-12-191 with valid Low THC Oil Registry card.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine (Schedule II controlled substance)
Amount was below 28g trafficking threshold
Possession was actual or constructive
enhancements: 28g or more: cocaine trafficking under § 16-13-31 with mandatory 10-year minimum
Near drug-free school zone: 2-year mandatory add-on
notes: Trafficking thresholds: 28g+ = 10 yrs mandatory; 200g+ = 15 yrs mandatory; 400g+ = 25 yrs mandatory.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine (Schedule II)
Amount was below 28g trafficking threshold
Possession was actual or constructive
enhancements: 28g or more: meth trafficking mandatory minimum 10 years
200g or more: 15-year mandatory minimum
400g or more: 25-year mandatory minimum
notes: Meth trafficking under § 16-13-31(e). Children present at meth lab triggers child endangerment charge.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed an opioid narcotic controlled substance (Schedule I-II)
No valid prescription or prescription was fraudulently obtained
Possession was actual or constructive
enhancements: 4g or more heroin: trafficking mandatory minimum 5 years
14g+ heroin: 10-year mandatory minimum
28g+ heroin: 25-year mandatory minimum
notes: Fentanyl treated as Schedule II. Distribution causing death may support felony murder under § 16-5-1(b).

statute_title: Possession of Prescription Drug Without Valid Prescription
elements: Defendant possessed a prescription controlled substance
Defendant lacked a valid, current prescription for the substance
Substance was on Georgia's controlled substance schedule
enhancements: Forged or altered prescription: fraud charges under § 16-13-73
Large quantity: trafficking presumption
notes: Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) data under § 16-13-57 frequently used as evidence.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed, sold, delivered, or manufactured a controlled substance
Quantity met or exceeded the statutory trafficking threshold for the specific substance
Defendant had knowledge of the nature of the substance
mandatory_minimum: 5-25 years depending on substance and quantity; no parole, probation, or suspended sentence on mandatory term
enhancements: Trafficking within drug-free zone: additional mandatory time
Leadership role: enhanced sentence
notes: No parole, probation, or suspended sentence on the mandatory minimum portion. Thresholds vary by substance.

statute_title: Distribution or Sale of Controlled Substance
elements: Defendant sold, delivered, distributed, or dispensed a controlled substance
Substance was on the controlled substance schedule
Defendant acted knowingly and intentionally
mandatory_minimum: 1 year
enhancements: Distribution within 1,000 feet of school, park, or public housing: mandatory additional 2-year term
Distribution to a minor: enhanced penalty
Prior distribution conviction: enhanced maximum
notes: Drug-free zone enhancement under § 16-13-32.4 adds mandatory 2 years consecutive.

elements: Defendant manufactured, produced, prepared, or processed a controlled substance
Substance was listed on the controlled substance schedule
Acts were knowing and intentional
mandatory_minimum: 1 year
enhancements: Meth lab with children present: child endangerment added under § 16-12-1
Trafficking quantity manufactured: trafficking charges
notes: Meth lab cleanup costs may be assessed against defendant under GA environmental statutes.

elements: Defendant possessed an object defined as drug paraphernalia (pipes, syringes, scales, etc.)
Defendant intended to use paraphernalia in connection with a controlled substance
enhancements: Sale of paraphernalia to minor: felony under § 16-13-32.1
notes: Intent inferred from proximity to drugs, residue, and circumstantial evidence.

elements: Defendant obtained or attempted to obtain a controlled substance by fraud
Methods included forged prescription, false name, false statement to practitioner, or doctor-shopping
Defendant acted with knowledge of the fraudulent nature of the act
enhancements: Healthcare provider fraud: professional license revocation
Multiple fraudulent prescriptions: charges may stack per occurrence
notes: PDMP enrollment required for Schedule II-IV dispensing; patterns are reportable to law enforcement.

statute_title: Possession of Controlled Substance with Intent to Distribute
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
Defendant intended to distribute, sell, or deliver the substance
Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, or other circumstantial evidence
mandatory_minimum: 1 year
enhancements: Near school, park, or public housing: additional 2-year mandatory term
With firearm: additional weapons charges
Trafficking quantity: trafficking threshold charges
notes: Intent proven circumstantially — scales, individual baggies, large cash, and cell phone records all relevant.

penalty_max: Death penalty or life without parole
elements: Defendant caused the death of another human being
With malice aforethought, either express or implied
The killing was unlawful
mandatory_minimum: Life imprisonment
enhancements: Statutory aggravating circumstances: death penalty eligible
Law enforcement officer victim: aggravated sentence
Multiple victims: consecutive life sentences
notes: Georgia has the death penalty. Felony murder under § 16-5-1(b) charged when death occurs during commission of a felony.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
During commission of cruelty to children in the second degree under § 16-5-70(b)
Without malice aforethought
mandatory_minimum: 10 years
notes: Georgia second-degree murder is limited to child cruelty as predicate. General felony murder is § 16-5-1(b).

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
While in a sudden, violent, and irresistible passion
Resulting from serious provocation sufficient to excite such passion in a reasonable person
No cooling-off period elapsed between provocation and killing
mandatory_minimum: 1 year
notes: Heat-of-passion reduces murder to voluntary manslaughter. Provocation must be legally sufficient under GA case law.

offense_class: Felony (during commission of unlawful act); Misdemeanor (lawful act in unlawful manner)
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Without malice or intent to kill
During commission of an unlawful act other than a felony (felony version)
OR during a lawful act performed in an unlawful manner lacking due caution (misdemeanor version)
notes: Vehicular manslaughter charged separately as Homicide by Vehicle under § 40-6-393.

elements: Defendant attempted to commit a violent injury upon another person, or committed an act placing another in reasonable apprehension of immediately receiving violent injury
With a deadly weapon or object likely to or actually resulting in serious bodily injury
OR with intent to rob, rape, or murder
OR by discharging a firearm from a motor vehicle toward a person or occupied building
mandatory_minimum: 3 years if firearm used; 5 years if victim is public safety officer
enhancements: Victim is law enforcement officer: mandatory minimum 5 years no parole
Family violence context: family violence felony designation
Gang-related: RICO enhancement under § 16-14-4
notes: Mandatory 3 years if victim is public safety officer or crime committed at public transit station under § 16-5-21(b).

offense_class: Misdemeanor; High and Aggravated Misdemeanor (certain circumstances)
elements: Defendant attempted to commit a violent injury to another person
OR committed an act placing another in reasonable apprehension of immediately receiving a violent injury
Defendant had apparent present ability to carry out the act
enhancements: Victim is elder (65+): high and aggravated misdemeanor
Victim is pregnant and defendant knew: high and aggravated misdemeanor
Committed on public transit: high and aggravated misdemeanor
notes: No physical contact required — apprehension of injury alone is sufficient for assault in Georgia.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (1st offense); Felony (2nd+ offense against same victim)
elements: Defendant intentionally caused substantial physical harm to another person
OR intentionally made physical contact of an insulting or provoking nature with another person
Act was knowing and intentional
enhancements: Second battery conviction against same victim: felony
High and aggravated misdemeanor if against elder, pregnant woman, or committed on public transit
notes: Simple battery under § 16-5-23 requires only insulting physical contact. Battery § 16-5-23.1 requires substantial physical harm.

elements: Defendant maliciously caused bodily harm to another person
By depriving them of a member of the body
OR by rendering a member of the body useless
OR by seriously disfiguring the body or a member thereof
mandatory_minimum: 5 years if victim is a public safety officer
enhancements: Victim is law enforcement or public safety officer: mandatory minimum 5 years
Use of caustic substance: enhanced penalty
notes: Serious disfigurement includes permanent scarring. Permanent loss of use of a limb qualifies.

elements: Defendant took property of another
From the person or immediately from the presence of another
By use of force, intimidation, threat, or placing the victim in fear
With intent to commit theft
enhancements: Victim 65 or older: mandatory minimum 5 years
Armed robbery: enhanced charge under § 16-8-41
notes: Distinct from theft — requires taking from person or presence with force or fear. Sudden snatching charged separately under § 16-8-40(b).

elements: Defendant took property of another
From the person or immediately from the presence of another
By use of an offensive weapon or any replica having the appearance of such a weapon
With intent to commit theft
mandatory_minimum: 10 years mandatory; no parole, probation, or suspended sentence on the mandatory portion
enhancements: Firearm used: no parole or early release on minimum term
Victim 65 or older: additional mandatory time
Multiple victims: consecutive sentences
notes: Imitation or replica firearm qualifies as offensive weapon. Home invasion robbery treated as armed robbery.

penalty_max: 20 years; life if victim is child under 14 and unrelated to defendant
elements: Defendant abducted or stole away any person without lawful authority
Held such person against their will
Act involved movement of the victim (asportation)
mandatory_minimum: 10 years; life if victim is child under 14 and defendant is not a parent
enhancements: Ransom demand: mandatory life imprisonment
Sexual assault during kidnapping: consecutive charges
notes: Slight movement (asportation) sufficient. Parental kidnapping charged separately under § 16-5-45.

elements: Defendant knowingly damaged by fire or explosive
Any building, structure, or dwelling
Without consent of the owner OR with intent to defraud insurer
enhancements: Person endangered or harmed: enhanced penalty
Insurance fraud motive: fraud charges added
Second-degree arson (§ 16-7-61): non-dwelling property, 1-10 years
notes: Second-degree arson covers vehicles and personal property. Third-degree (§ 16-7-62) covers woodland and brush fires.

elements: Defendant took a substantial step toward committing murder
With the specific intent to commit murder
The act was beyond mere preparation
enhancements: Firearm used: mandatory additional time under § 17-10-6.1
Victim is law enforcement: enhanced penalty
Gang-related: RICO enhancements
notes: Attempted felony punishable by 1-30 years. Courts impose substantial sentences for attempted murder.

statute_title: Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon
elements: Defendant committed an assault on another person
With a deadly weapon or any object which, when used offensively, is likely to or actually does result in serious bodily injury
mandatory_minimum: 3 years if a firearm was used; 5 years if victim is a public safety officer
enhancements: Firearm used: mandatory minimum 3 years no parole
Victim is law enforcement: mandatory minimum 5 years no parole
Vehicle used as deadly weapon: qualifies
notes: Vehicle can constitute a deadly weapon when used to strike a person.

elements: Defendant unlawfully took or appropriated property belonging to another person
With intention of depriving the owner of the property
enhancements: Value $5,000-$24,999: 1-5 years felony range
Value $25,000+: 2-10 years felony range
Theft from elder: aggravating factor
notes: GA felony threshold is $1,500. Multiple items may be aggregated if part of a common scheme.

elements: Defendant unlawfully took property of another
Property value was $1,500 or more
With intent to deprive owner permanently
enhancements: Value $25,000+: 2-10 years mandatory range
Theft from elder: enhanced sentencing
notes: Georgia does not use 'grand theft' as a formal label — this is felony theft by taking under § 16-8-2.

elements: Defendant unlawfully took property of another
Property value was under $1,500
With intent to deprive owner permanently
enhancements: Prior theft convictions: aggregate charges may reach felony threshold
notes: Georgia does not use 'petty theft' as a formal label — this is misdemeanor theft by taking.

elements: Defendant concealed or took possession of merchandise of a retail establishment
OR altered or transferred a price tag or moved merchandise between containers
With intent to deprive the merchant of possession or full retail value
enhancements: Organized retail crime with 3+ participants: felony regardless of value
3rd conviction within 5 years: felony
Booster bag or electronic shielding device used: enhanced charge
notes: Civil demand statute allows merchants separate recovery. Merchant detention privilege under § 16-8-14(d).

elements: Defendant entered or remained within a building, structure, vehicle, railroad car, watercraft, or aircraft
Without authority
With intent to commit a felony or theft therein
mandatory_minimum: 1 year (1st degree residential); 2 years (2nd offense)
enhancements: Residential dwelling (1st degree): minimum 1 year mandatory
Prior burglary conviction: 2-year minimum
Armed during burglary: additional weapons charges
notes: No breaking-and-entering required — unlawful remaining with felonious intent is sufficient.

statute_title: Burglary in the First Degree — Residential
elements: Defendant entered or remained in a dwelling house of another
Without authority
With intent to commit a felony or theft therein
mandatory_minimum: 1 year mandatory
enhancements: Victim present in dwelling at time of burglary: significant sentencing enhancement
2nd burglary offense: 2-year minimum
notes: Dwelling must be used for habitation. Unoccupied vacation home still qualifies as a dwelling.

statute_title: Burglary in the Second Degree — Commercial
elements: Defendant entered or remained within a building or structure other than a dwelling
Without authority
With intent to commit a felony or theft therein
enhancements: Prior burglary: enhanced sentence
Weapon possessed: additional charges
notes: Second-degree burglary covers commercial structures. Carries lesser penalty than residential burglary.

elements: Defendant unlawfully took or appropriated a motor vehicle belonging to another person
With intent to permanently deprive the owner of possession
enhancements: Carjacking (vehicle taken from person by force): armed robbery charges
Vehicle used in commission of another felony: additional charges
notes: Joyriding without intent to permanently deprive is lesser offense of theft by conversion under § 16-8-7.

elements: Defendant received, disposed of, or retained stolen property
Defendant knew or should have known the property was stolen
Intent to deprive the rightful owner
enhancements: Value over $25,000: enhanced felony sentence
Motor vehicle: automatic felony regardless of value
notes: Knowledge inferred from suspicious circumstances. Recent possession of stolen property creates an inference.

offense_class: Felony (1st degree, $500+ or reckless safety disregard); Misdemeanor (2nd degree, under $500)
penalty_max: 10 years (1st degree felony); 12 months (2nd degree misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused damage to property of another
Without consent of the owner
Damage equaled $500 or more (1st degree) OR defendant acted with reckless disregard for safety
enhancements: Public utility or critical infrastructure: enhanced penalty
Religious institution: potential hate crime enhancement under § 17-10-17
notes: First-degree under § 16-7-22 requires $500+ damage or reckless endangerment. Second-degree under § 16-7-23.

elements: Defendant entered the land or premises of another person
For an unlawful purpose OR without being invited, licensed, or privileged to do so
OR remained on property after being asked to leave by an authorized person
enhancements: Critical infrastructure trespass: felony under § 16-7-23.3
notes: Notice may be posted signs, verbal notice, or prior written notice. Physical force or breaking not required.

offense_class: Felony or Misdemeanor depending on damage amount
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Georgia uses 'criminal damage to property' rather than 'criminal mischief.' Damage amount determines classification.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (1st offense); Felony (2nd+ offense against any family or household member)
elements: Defendant committed battery against a family member or household member
Victim was spouse, former spouse, parent, child, person sharing same household, or person having child in common
Act was intentional and caused substantial physical harm or physical contact of insulting or provoking nature
enhancements: 2nd+ family violence conviction: felony classification
Aggravated assault or aggravated battery in family violence: felony on first offense
notes: Mandatory arrest policy in many GA jurisdictions. State may proceed without victim cooperation.

elements: Defendant intentionally caused substantial physical harm or made provoking contact
Against a family or household member as defined in the Family Violence Act
enhancements: Violation of TPO concurrent: additional charge
Child witness: aggravating sentencing factor
notes: Family violence designation triggers federal firearms prohibition under 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(9).

statute_title: Contributing to the Delinquency or Deprivation of a Minor
offense_class: Misdemeanor; Felony if serious injury or death results
penalty_max: 12 months (misdemeanor); 20 years (felony with serious injury or death)
elements: Defendant caused or encouraged a minor to violate any law
OR committed acts causing or likely to cause a minor to become delinquent, unruly, or deprived
Victim was a child under 18
enhancements: DUI with child under 14 in vehicle: additional misdemeanor under § 40-6-391(l)
Serious injury or death resulting: felony charges
notes: Child cruelty under § 16-5-70 more appropriate when physical abuse is involved.

elements: Defendant maliciously caused a child under 18 cruel or excessive physical or mental pain (1st degree)
OR parent or guardian willfully deprived a child of necessary sustenance to the extent health was jeopardized (2nd degree)
Act was knowing and intentional
mandatory_minimum: 5 years (1st degree cruelty to children)
enhancements: Death resulting from abuse: murder or felony murder charges
Pattern of repeated abuse: aggravating sentencing factor
notes: 1st degree requires malicious intent. 2nd degree under § 16-5-70(b) involves willful deprivation.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (1st offense); High and Aggravated Misdemeanor (2nd offense); Felony (3rd+ offense)
elements: A valid protective order or temporary protective order had been issued against the defendant
Defendant had actual knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully violated specific terms of the order
enhancements: Violence committed during violation: additional assault or battery charges
3rd violation: felony classification
notes: Order must be properly served, or defendant must have actual knowledge. Constructive knowledge insufficient in Georgia.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (1st offense); Felony (2nd+ offense or aggravated)
elements: Defendant followed, placed under surveillance, or contacted another person
Without consent and for the purpose of harassing and intimidating that person
Contact occurred at or near their home, workplace, school, or location they regularly frequent
enhancements: 2nd conviction: felony
Aggravated stalking (§ 16-5-91) — violation of court order: felony, 1-10 years
notes: Aggravated stalking charged when defendant violates bond, protective order, or probation/parole condition.

elements: Defendant made telephonic, electronic, or written contact with another person
With intent to harass, annoy, or alarm that person
Contact was unwanted
enhancements: Threat of violence included: terroristic threats charge under § 16-11-37
2nd offense: enhanced misdemeanor
notes: Separate from stalking which requires a surveillance or following pattern.

statute_title: Exploitation of Elder Person or Disabled Adult
elements: Defendant knowingly and willfully exploited, abused, or neglected an elder person (65+) or disabled adult
OR a caretaker neglected the basic needs of a person in their care
Act caused physical or financial harm
enhancements: Caregiver in position of trust: enhanced sentencing
Financial exploitation over $1,500: felony theft charges added
notes: Mandatory reporting required for healthcare workers and care facilities.

offense_class: Misdemeanor or Felony depending on location
elements: Defendant carried or possessed a firearm or weapon
In a location where carrying is prohibited (schools, government buildings, courts, polling places)
With knowledge of possession
enhancements: Carrying in school safety zone: felony under § 16-11-127.1
Armed during commission of felony: mandatory add-on under § 17-10-6.1
notes: Georgia enacted permitless carry (HB 218, April 2022) for eligible persons. Prohibited locations still constitute offenses.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm or Knife by Convicted Felon
elements: Defendant was convicted of a felony
Defendant received, possessed, or transported any firearm or knife with blade 3 inches or more
Defendant had actual or constructive possession with knowledge
mandatory_minimum: 1 year mandatory; 5 years if prior conviction was a violent felony
enhancements: Prior violent felony: mandatory 5 years no probation
Federal concurrent: 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1)
notes: Rights restoration possible only through full pardon. Also applies to certain family violence misdemeanants.

statute_title: Carrying in Prohibited Location — Weapons Carry License Context
elements: Defendant carried a weapon in a location prohibited by statute
Location included courthouse, polling place, government building, or school zone
Defendant had knowledge of the prohibited status of the location
enhancements: School zone: felony under § 16-11-127.1
notes: Georgia permits constitutional/permitless carry since April 2022. Carrying in specific prohibited locations remains an offense.

statute_title: Discharge of Firearm Near Public Highway or Street
elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
On or within 50 yards of a public road or highway
Across, into, or upon the road or right-of-way
enhancements: Shooting from a vehicle toward another: aggravated assault charges
Injury to another: battery or aggravated battery charges
notes: Separate provisions for discharge in incorporated areas. Reckless discharge covered under O.C.G.A. § 16-11-104.

elements: Defendant transferred, sold, or disposed of a firearm to a person known to be a prohibited possessor
OR engaged in unlicensed dealing in firearms as a business
With knowledge of the prohibited nature of the transaction
enhancements: Straw purchase for felon: federal charges
Ghost guns or untraceable firearms: enhanced federal penalty
notes: Large-scale firearms trafficking typically prosecuted federally under 18 U.S.C. § 922.

statute_title: Possession of Machine Gun, Sawed-Off Firearm, or Silencer
elements: Defendant possessed a machine gun, sawed-off rifle, sawed-off shotgun, or silencer
Weapon was not properly registered under the National Firearms Act
Defendant had actual or constructive possession with knowledge
mandatory_minimum: 2 years
enhancements: Use in commission of a crime: additional charges
Federal NFA violation: concurrent federal felony charges
notes: NFA-registered weapons are legal. State felony applies to unregistered NFA items.

elements: Defendant used a computer or telecommunications device
To obtain money, property, or services through fraudulent means
With intent to defraud
enhancements: Financial institution victim: enhanced federal penalties
Large monetary amount: enhanced sentence
Identity theft component: additional charges
notes: GA Computer Systems Protection Act under § 16-9-90 et seq. Federal wire fraud typically prosecuted in federal court.

elements: Defendant used the identifying information of another person
Without that person's consent
With intent to defraud
To obtain credit, goods, services, money, or to commit any felony
enhancements: 10 or more victims: enhanced felony penalty
Elder victim (65+): enhanced penalty
notes: § 16-9-121 covers financial identity fraud. § 16-9-122 covers identity fraud for non-financial purposes.

elements: Defendant lawfully obtained funds or property entrusted to them by another
Defendant converted the property to their own use
With intent to defraud the owner
Defendant was in a position of trust with respect to the property
enhancements: Public official or fiduciary: enhanced sentencing
Large amounts: enhanced felony tier
notes: Trust relationship distinguishes embezzlement from ordinary theft.

elements: Defendant made, altered, or possessed a writing
With intent to defraud
Writing appeared to be made by another person, or was falsely dated or fraudulently made to represent a different transaction
enhancements: Currency or government documents: enhanced penalty
Identity theft connected: additional charges
notes: First-degree forgery (§ 16-9-1): checks, credit cards, government IDs. Second-degree (§ 16-9-2): other commercial documents.

elements: Defendant made, possessed, or uttered counterfeit currency, securities, or other instruments
With intent to defraud
Items resembled genuine currency, securities, or instruments
enhancements: Federal currency counterfeiting: exclusive federal jurisdiction
Large amounts: enhanced federal penalty
notes: Currency counterfeiting is primarily a federal offense. State forgery statute covers counterfeit checks and documents.

elements: Defendant drew, made, uttered, or delivered a check or draft
Defendant knew at the time of issuance there were insufficient funds or no account
With intent to defraud the recipient
enhancements: Multiple returned checks: aggregated value may reach felony threshold
notes: 10-day notice provision: payment within 10 days of returned check notice may negate criminal intent.

elements: Defendant willfully failed to file a required tax return or pay taxes owed
OR willfully made false or fraudulent statements on a tax return
Act was knowing and intentional
enhancements: Large amount evaded: enhanced sentencing
Federal concurrent prosecution: 26 U.S.C. § 7201
Money laundering of tax proceeds: additional charge
notes: GA Department of Revenue enforces state tax crimes. IRS handles federal tax evasion.

elements: Defendant presented or caused to be presented a false or fraudulent claim to an insurer
OR made false statements in connection with an insurance application or claim
With intent to defraud the insurer
Claim was material to the insurance decision
enhancements: Healthcare insurance fraud: enhanced penalties
Organized fraud ring: RICO charges possible
Arson for insurance: additional arson charges
notes: Georgia Insurance Fraud Prevention Act under § 33-1-9. Insurance Commissioner investigates.

elements: Defendant used a credit card or credit card number without the cardholder's authorization
With intent to defraud the cardholder or issuer
Obtained goods, services, or money thereby
enhancements: Identity theft component: additional charges
Card skimming device used: enhanced penalty
notes: Georgia Credit Card Crime Law at § 16-9-31 et seq. covers manufacture, use, and trafficking in fraudulent cards.

penalty_max: 20 years or twice the value laundered, whichever is greater
elements: Defendant conducted a financial transaction involving proceeds of specified unlawful activity
Defendant knew the proceeds were derived from unlawful activity
With intent to promote unlawful activity OR to conceal the nature or source of the proceeds
enhancements: RICO connection: additional charges
Drug trafficking proceeds: federal parallel prosecution under 18 U.S.C. § 1956
notes: GA Banking and Finance Code § 7-1-922 is the state provision. Large cases typically prosecuted federally.

elements: Defendant obtained property of another by deceit
Defendant created or confirmed a false impression as to a past or present fact
Victim relied on the deception
Defendant intended to deprive victim of the property
enhancements: Elder victim (65+): enhanced penalty
Internet or wire used: computer fraud charges may be added
notes: Theft by deception under § 16-8-3. Covers false pretenses and fraudulent misrepresentation.

elements: Defendant knowingly executed or attempted to execute a scheme to defraud a financial institution
OR to obtain moneys or property owned by a financial institution by means of false pretenses
With intent to defraud
enhancements: During financial crisis or emergency: enhanced federal penalty
Identity theft component: additional charges
notes: Bank fraud typically prosecuted federally under 18 U.S.C. § 1344. State charges used for local institution cases.

elements: Defendant made an untrue statement of a material fact or omitted a material fact
In connection with the offer, purchase, or sale of a security
With intent to deceive and defraud investors
enhancements: Ponzi scheme: enhanced federal charges
Large number of victims: enhanced penalty
notes: Georgia Securities Act of 2008 governs state securities fraud. SEC handles federal securities fraud.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (1st offense); Felony (subsequent offense or victim under 16)
elements: Defendant intentionally made physical contact with the intimate parts of another person
Without the consent of that person
mandatory_minimum: 25 years if victim is under 16 (aggravated form); sex offender registration required
enhancements: Victim under 16: mandatory sex offender registration
Prior sex offense: enhanced mandatory sentence
notes: Sexual battery (§ 16-6-22.1) is misdemeanor for first offense. Aggravated sexual battery (§ 16-6-22.2) — object penetration — always felony.

elements: Defendant intentionally penetrated the sexual organ or anus of another person with a foreign object
Without the consent of that person
mandatory_minimum: 25 years mandatory minimum if victim is under 16; lifetime sex offender registration
enhancements: Prior sex offense: life imprisonment
Victim under 10: mandatory life
notes: Aggravated sexual battery covers penetration with a foreign object. Rape (§ 16-6-1) covers penile penetration.

elements: Defendant had carnal knowledge of a female
Forcibly and against her will
OR victim was under 10 years of age (per se regardless of consent)
mandatory_minimum: 25 years mandatory; lifetime sex offender registration
enhancements: Victim under 16: life imprisonment possible
Prior rape conviction: mandatory life imprisonment
notes: GA rape statute covers penile-vaginal penetration. Other penetration offenses covered by aggravated sexual battery (§ 16-6-22.2).

elements: Defendant performed an act of sexual intercourse or exposed genitals in a lewd and lascivious manner
In a public place
In the presence of or likely to be observed by another person
enhancements: 3rd conviction: felony and sex offender registration may be required
Exposure to a minor: enhanced charges
notes: Third conviction may trigger sex offender registration under § 42-1-12.

elements: Defendant performed or offered to perform sexual acts for money or other consideration (prostitution)
OR solicited another person to perform sexual acts for money (solicitation)
Exchange of consideration was part of the transaction
enhancements: Minor victim: trafficking in persons charges under § 16-5-46
Promoting prostitution or pimping: felony
notes: Sex trafficking of minors charged as trafficking in persons under § 16-5-46 regardless of force or coercion.

statute_title: Aggravated Sexual Battery / Computer or Electronic Pornography
penalty_max: 25 years (aggravated sexual battery); 20 years (child exploitation via digital means)
elements: Defendant used electronic or digital means to engage in or facilitate a sexual offense
OR digitally penetrated a victim without consent
Acts were knowing and intentional
enhancements: Child victim: child exploitation statutes apply
Online solicitation of minor: O.C.G.A. § 16-12-100.2
notes: Online solicitation of a child for sexual purposes under § 16-12-100.2 — separate statute.

elements: Defendant employed, used, persuaded, or coerced a minor to engage in sexually explicit conduct for visual depiction
OR knowingly possessed, distributed, or transmitted visual depictions of minors in sexually explicit conduct
Minor was under 18 years of age
mandatory_minimum: 5 years mandatory; lifetime sex offender registration
enhancements: Production: higher sentencing range than possession
Large quantity: each image or video may be a separate count
Federal concurrent: 18 U.S.C. § 2252
notes: Federal charges typically concurrent. Internet transmission explicitly covered.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender under Georgia law
Defendant failed to register or failed to update registration within required time
Defendant had actual notice of the registration requirement
mandatory_minimum: 1 year; 5-year minimum for 2nd offense
enhancements: 2nd offense: mandatory minimum 5 years
Absconding from supervision jurisdiction: 10-year minimum
notes: Residency restrictions under § 42-1-15 also apply (school, church, park proximity).

penalty_max: 20 years; life if defendant is 21+ and victim is under 14
elements: Defendant had sexual intercourse with another person under 16 years of age
Consent is not a defense
Defendant was 21 or older (for enhanced mandatory minimum)
mandatory_minimum: 10 years mandatory if defendant is 21+ and victim is under 14
enhancements: Defendant 21+ with victim under 14: 10-year mandatory minimum
Position of trust or authority: aggravating factor
notes: No close-in-age exemption in GA. Any sexual intercourse with a person under 16 is statutory rape regardless of defendant's age.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (1st offense against adult); Felony (subsequent offense or victim under 16)
elements: Defendant intentionally made physical contact with the intimate parts of another person
Without the consent of that person
enhancements: Victim under 16: felony with possible mandatory registration
Position of authority over victim: aggravating factor
notes: Intimate parts defined as genitals, buttocks, groin, inner thighs, or female breasts.

elements: Defendant acted in a violent, tumultuous, or boisterous manner
OR used obscene language in the presence of a minor causing reasonable fear of injury
OR acted in a manner creating loud and unreasonable noise disturbing the tranquility of others
OR used fighting words likely to provoke an immediate breach of peace
notes: Must be applied carefully to avoid First Amendment violations. Fighting words doctrine governs speech-based charges.

statute_title: Obstruction of a Law Enforcement Officer
elements: Defendant knowingly and willfully obstructed or hindered a law enforcement officer
In the lawful discharge of the officer's official duties
By act or omission
enhancements: Violence against officer: felony, 1-5 years
Injury caused to officer: aggravated penalty
notes: Providing a false name to an officer also constitutes obstruction. Non-violent refusal may still qualify as misdemeanor obstruction.

offense_class: Misdemeanor or Felony depending on conduct
elements: Defendant obstructed, hindered, or opposed a law enforcement officer or judicial proceeding
Act was knowing and intentional
Officer or proceeding was lawful
enhancements: Evidence tampering under § 16-10-94: separate felony
Witness intimidation under § 16-10-93: felony
notes: False statements to officers during investigation covered under § 16-10-20.

elements: Defendant was subject to a valid court order
Defendant willfully failed to comply or engaged in conduct disrupting judicial proceedings
Court had jurisdiction to issue the order
enhancements: Repeated contempt: consecutive penalties
notes: Direct contempt (in court) vs. indirect contempt (outside court). Criminal contempt requires proof beyond reasonable doubt.

elements: Defendant appeared in a public place in an intoxicated condition caused by alcohol or drugs
Intoxication manifested by boisterous or indecent conduct, or loud and profane discourse
notes: Simple intoxication in public is not a crime in GA without the disorderly conduct element.

elements: Defendant loitered or prowled in a place, at a time, or in a manner not usual for law-abiding individuals
Under circumstances that warranted alarm for the safety of persons or property in the vicinity
Defendant refused to identify themselves and explain their presence when requested by an officer
notes: Officer must request identification before arrest. Defendant must have opportunity to explain before being arrested.

elements: Defendant, together with others, engaged in tumultuous conduct
OR incited others to engage in tumultuous or unlawful conduct
Conduct created a public disturbance
notes: Riot charges under § 16-11-33 for 2+ persons using force or violence. Incitement to riot under § 16-11-31.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (misdemeanor underlying charge); Felony (felony underlying charge)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or bond for a pending criminal matter
Defendant had notice of the scheduled court appearance
Defendant failed to appear without lawful excuse
enhancements: Flight across state lines: federal failure to appear under 18 U.S.C. § 3146
notes: Criminal FTA is a standalone offense. Bench warrant issued upon failure to appear.

elements: Defendant made a report to law enforcement or emergency services
Defendant knew the report was false
Report described a crime or emergency that did not occur
enhancements: Swatting: enhanced penalty under § 16-10-26.1 (added 2019)
notes: False fire or bomb threats charged separately under § 16-10-33.

offense_class: Felony (threat of violence); Misdemeanor (threat to property)
elements: Defendant threatened to commit a crime of violence against another person or group
OR threatened to release a hazardous substance with intent to terrorize
Threat placed victim in reasonable apprehension of serious bodily injury
enhancements: Threat against a school: enhanced penalty
Electronic transmission: cyberstalking or cyberterrorism enhancement
notes: Threats of violence are felony under § 16-11-37(b). Bomb threats may be misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant was lawfully placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was willful
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation: revocation plus new charges
notes: Court may modify, continue, or revoke. Preponderance of evidence standard at revocation hearing.

elements: Defendant was on probation
Defendant failed to comply with a non-criminal technical condition such as failure to report, failure to pay fines, or positive drug test
notes: GA reformed technical violations to limit revocation for non-criminal violations. Short confinement periods may apply.

statute_title: Substantive Probation Violation — New Criminal Offense
offense_class: Probation revocation plus new criminal charge
penalty_max: Balance of original sentence + new sentence
elements: Defendant was on probation
Defendant committed a new criminal offense while on probation
New offense constitutes a violation of probation conditions
notes: Revocation hearing uses preponderance standard. New criminal charge uses beyond reasonable doubt standard.

penalty_max: Return to prison for remainder of original sentence
elements: Defendant was on parole
Defendant violated conditions of parole
Georgia Board of Pardons and Paroles determined violation warranted revocation
notes: GA Board of Pardons and Paroles has exclusive authority over parole revocation.

statute_title: Violation of Special Probation / Intensive Probation
elements: Defendant was on intensive probation or special conditions probation
Defendant violated specific conditions of the intensive supervision program
Violation was willful
notes: Georgia uses intensive probation supervision (IPS) for high-risk offenders. Violation triggers revocation hearing.

offense_class: Same felony class as target offense; Misdemeanor if target offense is misdemeanor
penalty_max: Same maximum as completed target offense
elements: Two or more persons agreed to commit an offense
Defendant was a party to the agreement
At least one overt act was committed in furtherance of the conspiracy
Defendant had specific intent to carry out the objective
enhancements: Drug trafficking conspiracy: mandatory minimums of underlying trafficking statute apply
RICO predicate: gang statute enhancement under § 16-14-4
notes: Overt act required in Georgia. Each co-conspirator liable for acts of others in furtherance. Withdrawal is an affirmative defense.

statute_title: Georgia RICO — Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations
fine_max: $25,000 or three times the proceeds derived
elements: Defendant was associated with an enterprise
Defendant conducted or participated in the affairs of the enterprise through a pattern of racketeering activity
Pattern consisted of at least two predicate acts within a 4-year period
Predicate acts were defined criminal offenses under § 16-14-3
mandatory_minimum: 1 year
enhancements: Gang activity as enterprise: concurrent street gang terrorism charges under § 16-15-4
Murder as predicate: life imprisonment possible
Asset forfeiture: mandatory
notes: Georgia RICO is broader than federal RICO. Widely used in gang prosecutions. Asset forfeiture available.

elements: Defendant used force against another person
Defendant reasonably believed force was necessary to defend against imminent unlawful force
Defendant was not the initial aggressor
Under Stand Your Ground: no duty to retreat if defendant is in any place they have a legal right to be
notes: Georgia has a broad Stand Your Ground law. Immunity hearing available before trial under § 16-3-24.2. Castle Doctrine under § 16-3-23 provides additional protection inside the home.

elements: Elements specific to each offense as defined under the Georgia Official Code Annotated
notes: Catch-all for Georgia offenses not otherwise enumerated. Consult the specific O.C.G.A. section for elements, penalties, and defenses.
